title: NCT vs ICT Tendering in Bangladesh
text:
In Bangladesh public procurement, tenders are run as NCT (National Competitive Tendering) or ICT (International Competitive Tendering). Both are published and managed on the e-GP portal under the Public Procurement Act 2006 and the Public Procurement Rules (PPR) 2025, administered by BPPA.






Warning



Here ICT means International Competitive Tendering. It is unrelated to the ICT Division (Information and Communication Technology), which is mentioned below only as a place that posts tech tenders.



Key Differences








Feature
NCT (National)
ICT (International)




Aimed at
The domestic market
Foreign as well as domestic suppliers and contractors


Tender document fee
Paid in BDT
Tk 12,000 per tender (e-GP release, August 2025); an earlier release required USD


Tender security
In BDT
In USD (July 2024 e-GP release)


e-GP registration
Local tenderer registration
A separate international tenderer registration; fees listed as Tk 12,000 (registration) and Tk 5,000 (renewal)


Foreign bank details
Not needed
SWIFT code or routing number can be entered


SLT price screening
Applies
Does not apply (e-GP states SLT is for national tenders only)


Typical use
Routine goods, small-to-medium works, local services
Specialised goods, high-value or technology-intensive contracts



The “typical use” row is a rule of thumb. The choice for a given package follows the PPR and the procuring entity’s market assessment, not a fixed list.


Which Document Fits
BPPA publishes separate standard tender documents for national procurement (for example e-PW3 for works and e-PPS3 for physical services, both labelled “National”) and for international procurement. Pick the one that matches the package category and method.


Where to Find Tenders

e-GP portal: the official platform where both NCT and ICT packages are published.
Ministries and departments: the ICT Division and the Department of ICT post tenders for technology tools, networks and consultancy.
Aggregators: BDTender collects notices from the ICT ministry. It is a private site, so confirm every notice on e-GP.



Sources

e-GP portal: new features
BPPA: key changes in PPR 2025
PPR 2025 (BPPA, PDF)
BPPA standard tender documents







Note



Fees and currency rules come from e-GP release notes and can change. The PPR 2025 PDF could not be text-extracted, so the legal thresholds and minimum tender periods for NCT and ICT are not covered here. Check the rules before choosing a method.

title: Works vs Physical Services under PPR 2025
text:
The Public Procurement Rules (PPR) 2025, issued under the Public Procurement Act 2006 by the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA), came into effect on 28 September 2025 and replaced PPR 2008. Two of the changes BPPA lists matter here:

Physical services are now a distinct procurement category. Before, routine services were often squeezed into Goods or Works templates.
The ±10% price limit is removed for national works procurement.

The practical difference between Works and Physical Services comes down to what the contract leaves behind: a built or modified asset, or a service performed.

Comparison








Feature
Works
Physical Services




Core objective
Construction, civil engineering, rehabilitation or physical modification of a facility or asset
Services that are physically carried out but do not build or construct anything


Output
A built asset: road, building, bridge, water supply
A task or activity delivered, such as maintenance or logistics


Standard tender document
e-PW3 (Works, Open Tendering Method)
e-PPS3 (Open/Limited Tendering), e-PPS6 (Direct Procurement)


Pricing basis
Bill of Quantities
Activity Schedule, with Performance Specifications


Price screening
The ±10% limit no longer applies in national works
Significantly Low-priced Tender (SLT) test, in national tenders



Physical Services also differ from intellectual and professional services, which are about expertise and advice rather than physical execution.


Works
Works contracts cover construction and repair projects: roads, buildings, bridges, water supply and similar assets. BPPA’s e-PW3 is the standard tender document for works under the Open Tendering Method, and a new version was issued under PPR 2025.
The ±10% limit used to tie the acceptable range of national works bids to the official estimate. PPR 2025 removes it.


Physical Services
Physical Services are services delivered through physical work that do not involve construction. Typical illustrations are maintenance and operations of existing facilities and logistics. Which standard document applies depends on the method and the type of service:







Document
Covers




e-PPS3
National tenders for physical services, except hiring service personnel through outsourcing; Open or Limited Tendering; award to the lowest evaluated responsive tender


e-PPS6
Physical services under the Direct Procurement Method


e-PPS2
Hiring service personnel through the outsourcing policy



In e-PPS3 the employer states its needs in the Tender Data Sheet and Particular Conditions of Contract, and in two sections specific to this category: the Activity Schedule (tenderers price each activity) and the Performance Specifications.

Significantly Low-priced Tenders (SLT)
e-PPS3 screens out abnormally low prices with a formula. Among technically responsive tenders (at least two), it computes a weighted average of:

the official cost estimate (weight 0.20),
a recent national price index from e-GP awards for physical services (weight 0.30), and
the prices quoted by responsive tenderers (weight 0.50).

It then computes the weighted standard deviation of the quoted prices. The lower limit of acceptable prices is the weighted average minus one standard deviation. A tender below that limit is treated as financially non-responsive and rejected.



Caveats

e-PPS3 and e-PPS6 were posted by BPPA as preliminary working drafts, so details may change. Always download the current version.
The e-GP portal states that the SLT calculation applies only to national competitive tenders.

title: SRFP: The Standard Request for Proposal
text:
In procurement, SRFP stands for Standard Request for Proposal. It is a model bidding document used to select consultants and other providers of intellectual and professional services, such as IT development, auditing, engineering design or research.
Unlike a regular tender for goods or works, where price usually decides the outcome, an SRFP weighs technical quality alongside cost to find the most qualified provider.
In Bangladesh, the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA) publishes the SRFPs for procuring services under the Public Procurement Act 2006 and the Public Procurement Rules (PPR) 2025.

Core structure
An SRFP combines sections that stay fixed with sections the procuring entity completes for each assignment. The usual parts are:

Letter of Invitation (LOI): the formal invitation to shortlisted consultants.
Instructions to Consultants (ITC): how to prepare, structure and submit a proposal, and how it will be evaluated.
Proposal Data Sheet (PDS): the assignment-specific section, with deadlines, contact points and requirements.
Technical Proposal forms: templates for the firm’s experience, methodology, work plan and staff qualifications.
Financial Proposal forms: templates for fees, costs and the overall price.
Terms of Reference (TOR): the scope of work, objectives, deliverables and timeline the client expects.
Conditions of Contract (GCC and PCC): the legal framework for the resulting contract.



SRFP vs. Standard Tender Document








Feature
SRFP
Standard Tender Document (STD)




Primary use
Intellectual, professional and consulting services
Goods, works and physical services


Focus
Methodology, skills and quality of the solution, with cost
Technical compliance and price


Examples
Software implementation, project management, financial audit
Building a road, buying equipment, routine maintenance





SRFP codes on BPPA’s list
BPPA’s offline SRFP page lists the following documents. The code depends on who is being hired, whether the contract is lump sum or time-based, and, for firms, the contract value.

Scope

Contract type

Lump sum
